headline: Growth continues as Millrose diversifies beyond Lennar
summary_short: Millrose's Q2 2026 net income rose 11.6% y/y to $125.9M ($0.76 diluted EPS) as revenue grew 32.1% to $196.9M, while the company expanded to 19 builder/developer counterparties and raised its dividend for a sixth straight quarter to $0.77/share.
summary_long: Revenue rose 32.1% y/y to $196.9M, including about $284M of development loans repaid on day one and redeployed into new opportunities. Operating income grew 32.1% and net income 11.6% to $125.9M ($0.76 diluted EPS); the smaller net-income gain reflects higher interest expense on larger debt balances. AFFO was $127.6M ($0.77/share); the AFFO run rate of $0.80/share is at the high end of prior guidance (range not restated here). Millrose redeployed $1.1B into land acquisitions, added its first multifamily land-banking deal (with JPI), and grew Invested Capital outside Lennar by $117M q/q to $2.8B. Cash fell 30.6% q/q to $34.2M as redeployment outpaced homesite-sale proceeds; equity was flat at $5,851.8M. Total debt was $2.5B (~30% debt-to-cap).

drivers.explanation: Revenue and net income both grew as the counterparty base expanded to 19 relationships and Invested Capital outside the Lennar program rose $117M q/q, reflecting continued diversification and capital redeployment.

Growth came from option-fee income across an expanding builder base; the total also includes roughly $284M of development loans repaid on the first day of the quarter and redeployed into new opportunities.

Operating income grew in step with revenue (both +32.1% y/y) because total operating expenses, mainly the Invested-Capital-linked management fee, grew at a similar pace, leaving margin roughly unchanged.
Pretax income grew more slowly than operating income because interest expense nearly quadrupled y/y ($40.0M vs $10.3M) on larger debt balances, partly offset by higher interest income.
Net income tracked pretax income's rise; income tax expense fell y/y ($2.5M vs $4.8M) despite higher pretax income, providing a modest additional lift.
EPS growth mirrors the 11.6% net-income increase; diluted share count was essentially unchanged y/y (166.06M vs 166.03M shares).
Cash declined as roughly $1.1B redeployed into new land acquisitions and development funding modestly exceeded net cash proceeds from homesite sales and loan repayments during the quarter.
Equity was little changed q/q as retained net income was largely offset by dividends declared in excess of net income (distribution in excess of net income widened to $23.7M).
